body:
<!-- pr-reviewer: c14a0de764c988030e22e4e62d8d4650cc4c3b2e -->
Review of c14a0de (read-only: fixture moves, rest/rapids/hidden semantics read via git show; I did not build or run).

Verdict: clean, no blockers. One non-blocking observation.

Checked:
- Fixture geometry. Move indices are right: 0-4 slots, 5-10 the new bridge, 11 vertical, 12 the lateral rapid, so `RAPID = 12` is correct. The X 18 floor pass (disc X 15..21) stops at the ledge edge, and the Z 12.5 pass along X 17 (disc X 14..20) clears everything above 12.5. What stands in the rapid's footprint at Z 5 is only the strip X 14..15, Y -5..5 under the ledge (underside Z 10). So the Z 5 rapid still meets uncut stock under the ledge, and the Z 12.5 rapid is clean (pass height equals rapid height, within z_tol).
- "Under the ledge" is still convicted, but by the march as well as the hidden law. In `rapids.rs`, `bad = marched || hidden_along(..)`. The march sees the strip at surface 12.5 > 5, so it convicts on its own. The PR body admits this. The test still guards the rapid-in-stock verdict it names.
- Nothing was weakened into passing for the wrong reason. The conviction and the clean-above cases keep their asserts (`RapidInStock { at: RAPID }`, `is_empty`). The bare-post and no-model tests now use `rapid_cleared` (the X 17 bridge clears the whole footprint down to the floor). They are negative controls that were clean for the same reason before: no shadow, so the hidden law has nothing to say. `rapid_under` beside a bare post would also convict via the march, as the comment says.
- Test count: 11 `#[test]` on the branch, 11 on origin/main.
- The `hidden.rs` doc edit is accurate: the rapid is marched along its length, not at three points.

Non-blocking: the rapid arm of the hidden-stock law (`hidden_along`) is now not pinned by any test. For a flat tool on a straight lateral rapid the march subsumes it, so deleting the `hidden_along` call would leave `overhang_laws` green. The annulus arm (`hidden_in_annulus`, shank tests) is still pinned. A follow-up issue could add a fixture the march cannot see (ball/bull tip near the rim, per the PR note). No change needed here.

<!-- review-cost: estimated -->
**Estimated agent cost:** ~$0.15 (rough estimate from size: 59 changed lines)

No token usage was recorded for this PR, so this is calibrated from PRs with measured cost (our fix PRs, fix agent + review: median ~$1.20, ~$2.33 per 1,000 changed lines; floor $0.15, cap ~$3.60). For a contributor's PR it estimates what writing and reviewing it the way our agents work would cost, not what their session actually spent.

Blended upper estimate: 90 % input / 10 % output at list price (Opus 5.5 ~$5.60/M, Sonnet 5.5 ~$2.80/M, Haiku 5.5 ~$0.14/M). Cache reads make the real cost lower; main-session coordination isn't counted.
